s1.syndrome_frame: Acute abdominal syndrome with pancreatic involvement and worsening glycemic control in a patient with a history of diabetes and cardiovascular disease
salient_findings: Bloody diarrhea without abdominal pain or fever
Pancreatic swelling with a peripheral rim and narrowing of the main pancreatic duct on imaging
key_facts: 67-year-old man with a 3-year history of type 2 diabetes mellitus
Managed with metformin and glimepiride
Prior percutaneous coronary intervention for acute myocardial infarction 2 months earlier
40-year smoking history, quit after myocardial infarction
Four episodes of bloody diarrhea daily
No abdominal pain or fever
Normal white-cell count, bilirubin, and liver function tests
Plasma glucose rose from 258 mg/dL to 449 mg/dL
Hemoglobin A1c increased from 7.3% to 8.0%
Microalbuminuria of 50.7 mg/day
Anti–glutamic acid decarboxylase antibodies were negative
Elevated serum amylase and lipase
Contrast-enhanced CT and MR cholangiopancreatography showed pancreatic swelling and duct narrowing

shortlist.label: Autoimmune pancreatitis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated serum IgG4 and pancreatic swelling with duct narrowing

shortlist.label: Chronic pancreatitis
shortlist.why_kept: History of smoking and abdominal symptoms

shortlist.label: Pancreatic cancer
shortlist.why_kept: Pancreatic swelling and duct narrowing, potential cause of worsening glycemic control

shortlist.label: IgG4-related disease
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated serum IgG4 and involvement of pancreas

shortlist.label: Ulcerative colitis-associated pancreatitis
shortlist.why_kept: History of ulcerative colitis and pancreatic involvement

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with pancreatic swelling, elevated serum amylase and lipase, and duct narrowing, along with the absence of abdominal pain and the presence of other autoimmune-related conditions such as ulcerative colitis, suggests autoimmune pancreatitis. Additionally, the elevated IgG4 levels, although within the reference range, in the context of other findings, support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Chronic pancreatitis
rejected.why: The patient's lack of abdominal pain and the acute onset of symptoms do not support chronic pancreatitis.

rejected.label: Pancreatic cancer
rejected.why: There is no direct evidence of a mass or tumor in the pancreas, and the patient's symptoms and laboratory findings are more suggestive of an inflammatory process.

rejected.label: IgG4-related disease
rejected.why: While the patient has elevated IgG4 levels, the diagnosis of IgG4-related disease typically requires more systemic involvement and specific histopathological findings, which are not mentioned in the vignette.

rejected.label: Ulcerative colitis-associated pancreatitis
rejected.why: Although the patient has ulcerative colitis, the pancreatitis appears to be a distinct entity with its own set of characteristics, such as pancreatic swelling and duct narrowing, rather than a direct complication of the ulcerative colitis.
